Juan Cortés

Undergraduate researcher in computational fluid dynamics at the University of Tennessee Space Institute. Double-majoring in Mechanical Engineering and Physics at the University of Maryland.

What I Do

Research

Computational fluid-structure interaction simulation of bat flight with membrane perforations, using Firedrake and PETSc on HPC clusters.

Projects

Engineering projects spanning structural optimization, thermodynamic modeling, embedded systems, and prosthetic device development.

Experience

Research intern at UTSI, mechanical team co-lead for the Accessible Prosthetics Initiative, and STEM tutor in physics and engineering.

Computational FSI Simulation of Bat Flight

Investigating how membrane perforations in bat wings affect flight performance through fluid-structure interaction modeling. Extended and validated an existing FSI codebase at UTSI under Dr. Esteban Cisneros-Garibay.
